transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Aurora CISO), Derek Wu (Aurora Infra), Priya Nair (Aurora Legal), Ethan Park (App Dev)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick intros - I'm Samir from Redwood, AE, and with me is Lena, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya: Hi, Maya here. CISO at Aurora. Thanks for making time.
[00:13] Derek: Derek, infra manager, focusing mostly on networking and deployment constraints.
[00:18] Lena: Great to meet you all. We'll keep this focused on security posture and what you need to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[01:05] Samir: To kick off, can you walk us through Aurora's constraints - compliance, residency, encryption, that sort of thing?
[01:15] Maya: Sure. We're SOC 2 Type II in flight and need vendor evidence. We also have some ISO 27001 items and industry regs for some customers. Data residency: prefer US Gov region for certain customers, but generally US/EU. Also, SSO via Okta is standard, SCIM provisioning preferred, and we need RBAC mapping to our internal roles.
[01:35] Samir: Totally. Our hosted offering has SOC2 and basic ISO artifacts, dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and improved isolation, and private can be on-prem or VPC with customer-controlled network.
[01:45] Maya: What's the difference for audit logs and access between Hosted and Dedicated?
[01:52] Lena: Hosted: we provide tenant-scoped audit logs with retention options, you can export via syslog or to S3. Dedicated: logs are isolated per customer and you can request longer retention, and we also support pushing to your SIEM. Private: you control the logging endpoint entirely.

[02:40] Priya: On legal, we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest, and whether you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or HSM.
[02:48] Lena: We support envelope encryption, KMS integration, and BYOK for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports our managed KMS by default, and we offer a BYOK path for enterprise customers - we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and for Private we can accommodate HSMs.
[03:10] Maya: Are private keys ever seen by Redwood?
[03:13] Lena: With BYOK, the keys are in your KMS and we never persist plaintext keys. For HSM integrations in Private, keys stay on your hardware. There are implementation notes we'll share.

[04:00] Ethan: Quick operational q: what does RBAC look like? Can we mirror our roles?
[04:05] Samir: We have RBAC with role templates - admin, operator, dev, auditor - and you can map SAML groups to roles. We also support fine-grained route-level permissions if you need to restrict model access.
[04:20] Derek: How does SAML provisioning work? Does Redwood support SCIM for user sync?
[04:25] Lena: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Okta is in our docs and we have sample configs. Note, sometimes provisioning attributes get mappable differently - punctuation and claim names can vary so there are small mapping steps. We'll send the sample Okta config.

[05:10] Maya: Audit logs - we need immutable logs and tamper evidence for certain customers.
[05:15] Lena: For Dedicated/Private, we can stream to your SIEM or S3 with object locking as needed. Hosted includes event logs with write-once policies and signed integrity metadata, but for the highest assurance Dedicated with customer-side log ingestion is recommended.

[06:00] Priya: Data retention - can we set retention per-customer or per-model? We have legal hold workflows.
[06:08] Lena: You can configure retention policies per workspace and per model route. Legal hold: we support indefinite retention flags and exports. For hosted, retention beyond default windows may require contract add-ons. We'll share the retention config matrix.

[07:00] Derek: Network-wise, for Private, do you support VPC peering, private link, or IP allowlists for Hosted?
[07:07] Samir: All three: VPC peering for Private, AWS PrivateLink/Private Service Connect options for Dedicated in cloud providers, and IP allowlists for Hosted API. We'll need to see your networking diagrams for the PoC.

[08:00] Maya: Pen tests - do you have recent third-party pen test results?
[08:05] Samir: Yes, we have a recent pen test summary and remediation report. We'll attach the redacted full report and an executive summary.

[09:00] Ethan: Performance - we might start on Hosted for dev but Dedicated for production. Any constraints for KV cache and latency-sensitive workloads?
[09:08] Lena: For latency-sensitive workloads, Dedicated with pinned GPUs and tuned batch profiles gives predictable p99s. We also do prefix/KV cache for repeated context, and for largest gains we recommend Dedicated. Hosted can be bursty but we have SLOs and fallbacks.

[10:20] Maya: Regarding certifications, you said SOC2 and ISO - can you confirm scope?
[10:25] Samir: SOC 2 Type II covers infrastructure and operations for our hosted control plane and core runtime; Dedicated has covered controls but with customer isolation; Private sits outside our SOC scope but we provide deployment hardening docs and can support customer attestations. ISO 27001 scope details are in the pack.

[11:10] Priya: Contract-wise, we need DPA and terms for data deletion on contract termination.
[11:15] Samir: We'll include a draft DPA. For Hosted we delete data per retention policy and can provide certificate of deletion for customer-specified timelines. For Dedicated/Private we can include more stringent clauses.

[12:30] Derek: Any constraints around model weights - do you host customer models or are they run on shared images?
[12:36] Lena: Customer models are stored in encrypted object storage; on Dedicated they're in tenant-scoped buckets. Access to model weights is RBAC controlled; Private means you manage the storage.

[13:40] Maya: Ok, what about threat detection and incident response?
[13:45] Samir: We have IR runbooks, SOC tooling, and we can share our incident response playbooks. For enterprise deals we offer SLA-backed incident notification timelines and a designated support channel.

[15:00] Ethan: A small one - do you support client-side encryption or deterministic encryption for PII?
[15:07] Lena: We can support client-side encryption for inputs if you want to, but it impacts model utility. Deterministic encryption is tricky for model features, but for metadata fields it's doable. We'll outline tradeoffs in the security pack.

[16:30] Maya: About BYOK: are there key rotation constraints or rekeying flows we need to manage?
[16:36] Lena: For cloud KMS, standard rotation policies work. For HSM/BYOK with Private you'll control rotation. If you rekey, we have re-encryption steps; this is something we'll map out.

[18:00] Priya: Any background checks or vendor onboarding questionnaires you usually fill out?
[18:05] Samir: We typically fill SIG Lite and have a vendor security questionnaire template. We'll complete your vendor security form; attach it to the CRM.

[20:00] Derek: For the PoC, we'll want to run a 1-week workload test with our sample traffic. How do we size Dedicated?
[20:08] Lena: Share traffic profile and peak QPS, and we'll propose a Dedicated sizing. For quick benchmarking we can spin up a small Dedicated pool and run your sample - that will show p99 latency and token cost.

[22:00] Maya: Can you confirm where audit logs are stored and how long they persist by default?
[22:05] Lena: Default retention is 90 days for Hosted audit logs, but you can extend to 365 for Dedicated or longer with archive to your S3. Private: you manage retention.

[24:00] Samir: We'll attach links to our security pack, SOC2 artifacts, and the Okta guide in the follow-up.

[24:30] Ethan: Any red flags we should be aware of if we start hosted then migrate to Dedicated?
[24:35] Lena: Migration is straightforward; model artifacts and keys need to be re-pointed. There can be small tokenization/embedding differences across quantization profiles - we'll run validation tests.

[27:00] Maya: For sensitive customer data, would you recommend Private?
[27:06] Lena: If your compliance requires you to manage keys or network fully, Private is the safest. Dedicated gives strong isolation and BYOK which covers many enterprise requirements without full on-prem.

[30:00] Priya: Legal asks for sample contractual language around data deletion and subprocessing - can you provide samples?
[30:05] Samir: Yes, we'll share DPA snippets and subprocessor list.

[32:00] Derek: Ok, timeline wise - we plan to decide by end of month. We need security artifacts early next week.

[32:10] Samir: Action plan - we'll send the security pack and SOC2 docs by Friday, Lena will share SSO/SCIM details and RBAC samples, and we'll schedule a 60-minute SE deep dive to scope the PoC.

[35:00] Maya: Sounds good. One last question - do you support audit log integrity proofs or tamper-evident logs?
[35:05] Lena: We add signed checksums and can support append-only object locking in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we offer signed event digests on request.

[38:00] Ethan: We'll want to test encryption performance overhead in the PoC.
[38:05] Lena: Noted - we'll include a short benchmark plan.

[40:00] Samir: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and DPA and get the deep dive on the calendar.
[40:10] Maya: Thanks, appreciate it.
[40:15] Derek: Thanks all.
[40:20] Samir: Bye 

[42:00] End of call.

Notes/Links referenced: security pack (https://redwood-inference.com/security-pack), Okta SSO sample (attached in follow-up), SOC2 Type II report (attached), draft DPA (to be shared).
